formatNotes: 40 men and 40 women qualified via Open > Quarterfinals > Semifinals. Each event was worth a maximum of 100 points. The competition was profoundly altered on Day 1: Serbian athlete Lazar Dukic died during the swim portion of Event 1 (Lake Day), and the two remaining Day 1 events - 'Hammer Down' (4 rounds for time: 50 sledgehammer strikes with a 20/16-lb sledgehammer, 14 sandbag throws over a tire at 100/70 lb, 5 tire flips at 242 lb) and 'Amanda .45' (13-11-9-7-5 reps of muscle-ups and squat snatches, 12-minute cap) - were cancelled. Competition was paused and resumed Friday afternoon after consultation with athletes and the Dukic family. Roughly 13-16 athletes per the various reports withdrew in the following days, including reigning champions Laura Horvath and Jeffrey Adler, Lazar's brother Luka Dukic, Karin Freyova, Emma Tall, Elisa Fuliano, Victoria Campos, Sam Cournoyer, Guilherme Malheiros, Moritz Fiebig, Jacqueline Dahlstrom, Dani Speegle, and Arielle Loewen. The originally planned two cuts (to 30 after the Saturday morning event, to 20 by end of Saturday) were replaced with a single cut: the top 30 men and women after Saturday advanced to Sunday. 10 of the originally programmed 12 events were contested; events here are numbered 1-10 as actually contested (in original programming Chad was Event 7 and the Clean Ladder Event 8).
yearSummary: The 2024 Games in Fort Worth were defined by tragedy: Lazar Dukic drowned during the opening Lake Day swim-run, the rest of Day 1 was cancelled, and the event continued only after consultation with athletes and his family, with many competitors withdrawing in solidarity. The 10 contested events were a compressed version of the planned 12-event program, anchored indoors at Dickies Arena with offsite tests at Marine Creek Lake and Farrington Field. Programming spanned a 67-minute hero-workout grind (Chad 1000X, making its Games debut), an elimination-style clean ladder topping out at 365/250 lb, and back-to-back separately scored sprint finals with yoke carries. Tia-Clair Toomey-Orr, returning after the birth of her first child, won six of ten events and claimed a record-extending seventh title, while 22-year-old James Sprague emerged from a wide-open men's race - following the withdrawal of defending champion Jeffrey Adler - for his first title.

events.name: Lake Day
events.description:
For time:
3.5-mile run
800-meter open-water swim

Contested offsite at Marine Creek Lake, Fort Worth. Athletes completed the run first, then finished with the 800-m swim.
events.notes: Serbian athlete Lazar Dukic died during the swim portion of this event; his body was recovered later that day. The remaining two Day 1 events (Hammer Down and Amanda .45) were cancelled and the competition was paused until Friday afternoon. Victor Hoffer is recorded as withdrawn during the event. The tragedy prompted widespread scrutiny of event safety and water-rescue provisioning.

events.name: Midline Climb

50 deadlifts (225 lb M / 155 lb W)
3 rope climbs

3 rope climbs
50 GHD sit-ups
3 rope climbs
50 GHD sit-ups
3 rope climbs

events.notes: First event after competition resumed following Lazar Dukic's death; coverage described a restrained, respectful atmosphere as athletes returned. Source conflict: the official games.crossfit.com workout page and WODconnect list 3 rope climbs at each of the 5 rope stations (15 total); the Wikipedia event table summary lists 5 per station. Recorded as 3 per the official source.

events.name: Firestorm
events.description:
3 rounds for time:
15/11-cal Echo bike (M/W)
11 burpees over barricade

Time cap: 4 minutes (men) / 5 minutes (women)
events.notes: Time caps differed by gender: 4:00 for men, 5:00 for women (BarBend: 'aggressive time cap of five minutes for the women and four for the men'). The schema's single timeCapMin field cannot hold both, so it records the larger women's cap (5); the men's 4:00 cap is in the description. Australian Grace Walton took the women's event win.

events.name: Track and Field
events.description:
Two separately timed parts, one event score (combined placement across the parts). Contested Friday night offsite at Farrington Field.

Part 1 - For time:
1,600-meter run

Part 2 - begins at the 12:00 mark - For time:
50-yard sprint
50-yard sandbag carry (100 lb M / 70 lb W)
75-yard sprint
75-yard sandbag carry (100 lb M / 70 lb W)
100-yard sprint

Time cap: none on Part 1 (12-minute window before Part 2); 3 minutes on Part 2.
events.notes: Scored on combined rank of the two parts, so no single winning time exists; Garard and Toomey-Orr each won both parts outright. Fastest sprint-course (Part 2) times: Garard 1:04.89, Toomey-Orr 1:13.10; fastest 1,600-m times: Garard 4:55.13, Toomey-Orr 5:30.16. Contested under lights at Farrington Field in roughly 88 F heat. Event podiums: men Garard, Luke Parker, Roman Khrennikov; women Toomey-Orr, Haley Adams, Aimee Cringle.

events.name: Chad
events.description:
For time:
1,000 weighted box step-ups wearing a ruck (45 lb M / 35 lb W), 20-inch box
*Completed as 250 trips (4 step-ups per trip) along rows of boxes on the arena floor.

Time cap: 67 minutes

Run as one single mixed heat: all remaining men and women (32 men, 35 women) on the floor together at Dickies Arena on Saturday morning.
events.notes: First time the hero benchmark Chad 1000X was contested at the Games, honoring Navy SEAL Senior Chief Chad Wilkinson and raising awareness of veteran suicide. The official card reads only '1,000 step-ups (35/45 lb), completed as 250 trips'; the 20-inch box is the benchmark standard and reported by BarBend, with each trip counted as 4 reps across rows of boxes. This was Sprague's first individual Games event win and a springboard to his title.

events.name: Clean Ladder
events.description:
Elimination-style power clean ladder, three rounds, each round for time (2-minute working window per round).

Round 1 (all remaining athletes, ~30): 5 bars, reps 3-3-2-2-1
Men 255-265-275-285-295 lb / Women 165-175-185-195-205 lb
Top 20 advance.

Round 2 (20 athletes): 4 bars, reps 2-1-1-1
Men 295-305-315-325 lb / Women 205-215-225-230 lb
Top 10 advance.

Round 3 (10 athletes): 3 bars, reps 1-1-1
Men 325-345-365 lb / Women 230-240-250 lb

Final placement by round reached, then completion/time within the round.
events.notes: Medeiros was first to clean the 365-lb final bar (37.24), edging Bruno Marins (37.74) and Travis Mayer. Toomey-Orr won the women's final round at 250 lb in 25.05 over Kyra Milligan (25.15). The 30/20/10 advancement reflects the published structure; exact Round 1 athlete counts varied slightly due to withdrawals. Rounds were separately clocked with a 2-minute working window each; timeCapMin (6) is the sum of the three per-round caps per the schema convention.

events.name: Push Pull 2.0
events.description:
For time:
45 handstand push-ups
80-foot sled pull, standing (180 lb M / 110 lb W)
30 strict handstand push-ups
80-foot seated sled pull (from the platform)
15 freestanding handstand push-ups (advancing every 3 reps)

Time cap: 10 minutes
events.notes: Sequel to the 2014 'Push Pull' event. Rookie Lexi Neely won the women's field by 28 seconds, finishing the 15 freestanding handstand push-ups in two sets. Minor source conflict on Panchik's time: BarBend and The Barbell Spin list 6:20.80, FitnessVolt 6:31.80; recorded 6:20.80. The cut to the top 30 for Sunday was applied after this event.

events.name: Dickies Triplet
events.description:
5 rounds for time:
175-meter run
12 toes-to-bars
8 alternating dumbbell snatches (100 lb M / 70 lb W)

Time cap: 11 minutes
events.notes: Opening event of the final day, contested by the top 30 (less withdrawals) inside Dickies Arena, with the run laps weaving through the arena. Hopper's second event win of the week.

For time:
24 thrusters (95 lb M / 65 lb W)
24 chest-to-bar pull-ups
80-foot yoke carry (425 lb M / 245 lb W)

Followed by 2 minutes rest, then Final 1815 (separately scored).
events.notes: First half of the back-to-back GORUCK finals, each scored as its own 100-point event with 2 minutes rest between.

events.name: Final 1815
events.description:
For time (begins 2 minutes after completion of Final 2421):
18 thrusters (135 lb M / 95 lb W)
18 bar muscle-ups
80-foot yoke carry (525 lb M / 345 lb W)

Time cap: 7 minutes
events.notes: Hatfield swept both finals; Toomey-Orr's win sealed her record seventh title (951 points) while James Sprague (806) held off Dallin Pepper (785) and Brent Fikowski (765) for his first. Minor source conflict: The Barbell Spin lists Toomey-Orr at 4:40; BarBend and FitnessVolt list 4:33.89, recorded here.
